title: ～ような気がする — “I have a feeling that ～”
summary: Expresses a vague feeling or hunch that you cannot fully support: “I feel as if ～.” It attaches to the plain form of a verb or adjective (な-adj + な, noun + の). It softens a statement and is common in speech.

patterns.form: 普通形＋ような気がする

patterns.gloss: shorter form: I have a feeling ～

body.p: The speaker does not say “it is so,” only “I feel it is so.” どこかで彼に会ったような気がする: I can’t remember, but it feels like we met. 気 means “feeling”.
The form before ような shows the content: ta-form for a vague memory (聞いたような気がする), dictionary form for a premonition (起こるような気がする), and ている form for the present.
～と思う states a thought or opinion. ～ような気がする is more of an intuitive, uncertain feeling and sounds softer. For a firm judgment, use ～と思う or ～に違いない.

examples.ja: どこかで彼（かれ）に会（あ）ったような気（き）がする。
examples.romaji: Dokoka de kare ni atta you na ki ga suru.
examples.tr: I have a feeling I’ve met him somewhere.

examples.ja: 今夜（こんや）は何（なに）かいいことが起（お）こるような気（き）がする。
examples.romaji: Konya wa nani ka ii koto ga okoru you na ki ga suru.
examples.tr: I have a feeling something good will happen tonight.

examples.ja: この曲（きょく）は、前（まえ）にも聞（き）いたような気（き）がする。
examples.romaji: Kono kyoku wa, mae ni mo kiita you na ki ga suru.
examples.tr: I have a feeling I’ve heard this song somewhere before.

pitfalls: It is a subjective feeling, so the subject is normally the speaker (気がする, not 気がします for someone else).
Do not use it for facts you are sure of. It signals uncertainty.
